title: Large Payments Model
abstract: arXiv:2611.15814v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Payment applications such as fraud detection, authorization prediction, and payment optimization draw on overlapping transaction information. This motivates a reusable payments intelligence layer that shares learned representations and predictive signals, rather than developing predictive models independently for each task. Realizing this shared capability requires handling heterogeneous transaction fields, high-cardinality identifiers, lifecycle-dependent attributes, long histories, and rare outcomes while meeting latency and cost constraints. We present Large Payments Model (LPM), a domain-specific foundation model designed for operational use and trained from scratch on large-scale structured transaction data to learn reusable representations for payment prediction tasks. translated_abstract: 诸如欺诈检测、授权预测和支付优化等支付应用都依赖于彼此重叠的交易信息。这促使人们构建一个可复用的支付智能层，以共享学习到的表示和预测信号，而不是为每个任务独立开发预测模型。实现这种共享能力需要处理异构的交易字段、高基数的标识符、依赖生命周期的属性、漫长的历史记录以及罕见的结果，同时还要满足延迟和成本方面的约束。我们提出了大型支付模型，这是一个专为实际运营使用而设计的领域特定基础模型，它在大规模结构化交易数据上从零开始训练，以学习可用于支付预测任务的可复用表示。LPM 采用字段特定编码和生命周期感知的自监督学习，并包含两种互补的架构：独立变体使用混合掩码和支持……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文提出了大型支付模型（LPM），一个在大规模结构化交易数据上从零训练的领域专用基础模型，通过字段特定编码和生命周期感知的自监督学习，为欺诈检测、授权预测和支付优化等多种支付任务提供可复用的表示和预测信号。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Large Payments Model (LPM), a domain-specific foundation model trained from scratch on large-scale structured transaction data using field-specific encodings and lifecycle-aware self-supervision to learn reusable representations that power multiple payment prediction tasks such as fraud detection, authorization prediction, and payment optimization.
